requirement_paraphrase: Sets terminology, principles and methodology for risk assessment and risk reduction across machine life cycle, including documenting and verifying the process; basis for type-B and type-C standards. Excludes risk to domestic animals, property, environment.
notes: Generic risk method; environment excluded

requirement_paraphrase: Safety requirements for industrial robots as partly completed machinery: inherently safe design, risk reduction, information for use. Not applicable to underwater, law-enforcement, military, airborne/space, medical/healthcare or prosthetic robots, to service robots where the public has access, or to consumer products; not retroactive to robots made before publication.

Secondary summary: 2025 edition adds operating-mode requirements (lockable selector), robot Classes I and II, cybersecurity requirements to the extent they affect safety, and absorbs collaborative requirements formerly in ISO/TS 15066.
Safety requirements for industrial robot applications and cells across design, integration, commissioning, operation, maintenance, decommissioning and disposal, plus information needed at each stage.

instrument: ISO 10218-1/-2 and EU harmonisation
requirement_paraphrase: Vendor page says conformity to EN ISO 10218-1/-2 gives presumption of conformity once cited in OJ, and calls the 2025 harmonised editions 'expected'; also says risk-assessment reports should be kept 10 years and PFL contacts validated by measurement or simulation.

instrument: ISO/TS 15066
requirement_paraphrase: Technical specification giving safety requirements for collaborative industrial robot systems and the work environment, supplementing ISO 10218-1 and -2; edition 1 (2016), stage 90.92 since 2025-06-26, to be replaced by ISO/AWI 15066-1.

Safety requirements and verification for driverless industrial trucks, AGVs and AMRs: control system, guidance, automatic/manual/maintenance modes. Annex A covers operating-zone preparation; Annex B lists significant hazards. Excludes public zones (see ISO 13482), roads, explosive atmospheres and severe conditions.
notes: Severe conditions excluded; no hazard evidence asked

requirement_paraphrase: Covers robotic-function safety of service, communication, information, education and entertainment robots, indoor and outdoor, supplementing safety of the non-robotic function; excludes medical/care, industrial-only, people-transport, most food service, toys, hazardous-location robots.

instrument: SACE (University of York)
requirement_paraphrase: Eight-stage system-level process: operating context, hazardous scenarios, safe operating concept, safety requirements, design, hazardous failures, out-of-context operation (ODM boundary and minimum risk strategy), verification; each with a GSN pattern; ML components handled via AMLAS.
notes: Process steps only; no environmental hazard detail seen

instrument: Implementing Reg (EU) 2019/947 (as fetched from EUR-Lex PDF)
requirement_paraphrase: Operational risk assessment must describe the operation and environment, set safety objectives, identify ground and air risks, choose mitigations and determine required robustness; target safety level is equivalent to manned aviation. Mitigation types listed include containment, operational limits, procedures, competence and design features.
notes: Operator describes environment and picks mitigations

instrument: Implementing Reg (EU) 2019/947 (as fetched from EUR-Lex PDF) Annex Part A
requirement_paraphrase: Subcategories: A1 (C0/C1, avoid assemblies), A2 (C2, 30 m horizontal separation reducible to 5 m in low-speed mode, staged competency incl. 30-question exam), A3 (C2-C4 or private-built under 25 kg, at least 150 m from residential/commercial/industrial/recreational areas). Remote pilot competency requirements differ by subcategory.

instrument: Implementing Reg (EU) 2019/947 (as fetched from EUR-Lex PDF) Annex Part B
requirement_paraphrase: Authorisation application (UAS.SPEC.030) is based on the Art. 11 risk assessment and includes registration number, accountable manager (or operator name), the risk assessment, proposed mitigations in sufficient detail, an operations manual where risk and complexity require one, and insurance confirmation where required by law. Operator (UAS.SPEC.050) must establish procedures for safety, security, unlawful interference, data protection (DPIA where required) and noise/emissions, designate competent remote pilots, train staff, and keep records of operations.
notes: Unlawful interference procedures are security, not a named GNSS hazard

instrument: JARUS SORA Main Body Ed. 2.5 (JAR-DEL-SRM-SORA-MB-2.5)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommended OSOs with required robustness by SAIL I-VI (NR/L/M/H). OSOs listed in v2.5: #01, #02, #03, #04, #05, #06, #07, #08, #09, #13, #16, #17, #18, #19, #20, #23, #24. Examples: OSO#06 (C3 link) NR/L/L/M/H/H; OSO#04 (airworthiness design standard) NR/NR/NR/L/M/H; OSO#24 (adverse environmental design) NR/NR/M/H/H/H.
notes: OSO#24 robustness by SAIL; who sets conditions not shown

instrument: JARUS SORA Main Body Ed. 2.5 (JAR-DEL-SRM-SORA-MB-2.5)
requirement_paraphrase: SORA excludes carriage of people and dangerous goods; cyber security aspects, including protection from unlawful electromagnetic interference, are handled in a separate Cyber Safety Extension for Annexes B and E (not retrieved); privacy and environmental/financial aspects are outside the method; operator must still meet other regulatory requirements.
notes: Interference handled in separate extension, not retrieved

instrument: EASA AMC & GM to Reg (EU) 2019/947 (Annex to ED Decision 2025/018/R)
requirement_paraphrase: EASA AMC and GM to Reg (EU) 2019/947 (Issue 1, Amendment 3): OSO #08 covers defined, validated operational procedures; OSO #13 covers adequacy of external services supporting the operation. GNSS-specific text not confirmed.
notes: Title only; GNSS text not confirmed

instrument: EASA AMC & GM to Reg (EU) 2019/947 (Annex to ED Decision 2025/018/R)
requirement_paraphrase: OSO #23 requires environmental conditions for safe operation to be defined and measurable (robustness low at SAIL I-II, medium III-IV, high V-VI). OSO #24 requires the UAS to be designed and qualified for adverse environmental conditions (none at SAIL I-II, medium at III, high at IV-VI).
notes: Conditions defined by applicant; no values or method

instrument: FAA Part 107 Waiver Section Specific Evaluation Information
requirement_paraphrase: FAA waiver evaluators review the applicant's ConOps and hazard/risk analysis (severity, likelihood, mitigations, residual risk). For a 107.31 BVLOS waiver they check how the RPIC knows aircraft altitude/attitude/movement within C2-link limits, detects and avoids traffic, is alerted to degraded functionality, has the knowledge and skill, and which C2 links and FCC authorisations are used (BVLOS should not rely on FCC Part 5/15 devices). Under 107.25 (moving vehicle) lost-link behaviour must not create noncompliance. DAA evidence scales with risk: applicant statement and data (low), third-party validation plus an industry standard such as ASTM F3442 or RTCA DO-365 (medium), possible FAA/CAA certification (high).
notes: C2 link and lost link, no environmental hazard

instrument: Cabinet Resolution No. (110) of 2023
requirement_paraphrase: Certificate of conformity requires test reports from accredited laboratories covering 17 items: general design requirements, electrical safety, vibration/shock, EMC, GPS feature, safe fall/return/hovering, noise, MTOM, max altitude, range/endurance, horizontal speed, transmission power, geographical boundary identification, frequency compatibility, total flight time, response to government anti-drone interception systems, and collision-avoidance technology.
notes: Lab tests listed; EMC, vibration, GPS feature; no method named; no heat or dust item

instrument: GCAA CAR-UAR (Recreational UA Flights)
requirement_paraphrase: Recreational pilots must be 18+, UAE resident, register on the UAE Drones platform (drones.gov.ae) with UAE Pass, hold ATO training certificate, obtain a MOIAT product status statement, carry remote ID, stay under 5 kg and 400 ft, VLOS, daylight, obtain flight approval per flight, no cameras, no modifications.

instrument: GCAA CAR-UAS (UAS and Operations)
requirement_paraphrase: Issue 01 (issued 6 Feb 2018, applicable 4 Mar 2018) requires a UOA, with limits in UAS.030 (daytime, VLOS and VMC, 400 ft, 25 kg); UAS.020 sets a 50 m minimum safety distance; GM to UAS.045 mentions geo-fencing for segregated and non-segregated airspace; lost-link, GNSS and pilot licence are not addressed. UAS.025 is occurrence reporting (72 h), not operating limits.
notes: Paraphrase says GNSS not addressed

instrument: UAE information paper to MIDANPIRG/20 & RASG-MID/10 (ICAO site)
requirement_paraphrase: May 2023 UAE paper: daylight VLOS below 400 ft AGL with special approvals for other operations; mostly outside controlled airspace; zone map; existing CAR-UAC, UAD, UAEV, UAX, UAR under Federal Decree-Law 26/2022; planned CAR-Airspace, UTMSP, UTM and USP/ASP; GNSS and remote ID not mentioned.
notes: Paraphrase says GNSS not mentioned

instrument: Dubai RTA/DIEZ/talabat delivery robot pilot (news)
requirement_paraphrase: Three delivery robots run within about 3 km in a closely monitored environment; neither report names a permit, regulation or safety standard.

instrument: Safety Assurance Argument Templates for Autonomous Systems (Adelard for Dstl)
requirement_paraphrase: Provides argument templates incl. a safety-monitor architecture with environmental, health and behaviour guards, and ML-sensor arguments with confidence from real and simulated trials (headings seen); hazard analysis section suggests ODD validity/completeness could be assessed separately from hazard analysis of the intended function.
notes: Headings seen only

instrument: BSI PAS 1883 ODD taxonomy for an ADS
requirement_paraphrase: Gives a minimum hierarchical ODD taxonomy (scenery, environmental conditions, dynamic elements). Environmental attributes include wind, rainfall, snowfall, particulates (incl. airborne dust and sand) and illumination. Excludes test procedures and monitoring requirements for ODD attributes.
notes: Taxonomy attribute only; excludes test procedures

instrument: BSI PAS 1883 ODD taxonomy for an ADS
requirement_paraphrase: Temperature is only an optional extra weather attribute, not a defined attribute; glare is mentioned only as a detrimental effect in the illumination text, though sun elevation and position are illumination attributes (cl. 5.3.3); the term GNSS is not used - positioning is covered as Galileo/GLONASS/GPS under connectivity (5.3.4) with signal strength/interference as optional sub-attributes, and loss of positioning signal appears as an interference zone under scenery zones (5.2.2(e)).
notes: Describes silence on temperature, glare, GNSS

instrument: SAE J3016 Taxonomy and Definitions for Driving Automation
requirement_paraphrase: Defines ODD as operating conditions under which a driving automation system is designed to function, including environmental, geographical and time-of-day restrictions and/or required traffic or roadway characteristics; per Note 1, rapid transient changes (e.g. inclement weather) do not necessarily represent an ODD exit.
notes: Definition only

instrument: Toward an Agricultural Operational Design Domain: A Framework (arXiv 2511.02937)
requirement_paraphrase: Paper says existing ODD concepts do not yet address agriculture; Tables 1-2 include no dust visibility attributes of 50 m; GNSS appears in the digital information layer of Fig. 4 and is not in the tables.
notes: Paper says no dust attributes; GNSS only in a figure

instrument: AMLAS Guidance on Assurance of ML in Autonomous Systems
requirement_paraphrase: AMLAS expects data requirements covering relevance, completeness, accuracy and balance, with data validation results justifying gaps, and documents the operating environment; the named justification report and the word must were not confirmed.
notes: Must not confirmed

instrument: SACE Safety Assurance of autonomous systems in Complex Environments
requirement_paraphrase: Eight-stage process (operating context, hazardous scenarios, safe operating concept, safety requirements, design, hazardous failures, out-of-context operation, verification), each ending in a GSN pattern; the Operational Domain Model defines where safety is argued.
notes: Process steps only

instrument: Hoss, Scholtes, Eckstein - Review of Testing Object-Based Environment Perception
requirement_paraphrase: Notes that covering the ODD with test scenarios is hard, public datasets target diversity not safety relevance, simulation struggles to model sensor-environment interaction, and RTK-GNSS reference accuracy degrades near buildings/trees.
notes: Review of testing difficulties

instrument: UNECE WP.29 ADS regulation (as above)
requirement_paraphrase: UNECE WP.29 adopted (24 Jun 2026, reported) a regulation for fully driverless ADS built on a safety case and safety management system; manufacturers must show no unreasonable safety risk using credible testing, including validated virtual environments, proving-ground testing and real-world trials, plus in-service monitoring/reporting and a Data Storage System for Automated Driving. (Blog does not mention ODD or SAE levels.)
notes: Testing in general, no named hazard

instrument: JARUS SORA Main Body
requirement_paraphrase: Operational Safety Objective 23 (Table 14: 'Environmental conditions for safe operations defined, measurable and adhered to') is recommended at Low robustness for SAIL I-II, Medium for SAIL III-IV and High for SAIL V-VI.
notes: OSO#23 conditions defined, measurable, adhered to

instrument: JARUS SORA Main Body
requirement_paraphrase: OSO#24 (UAS designed and qualified for adverse environmental conditions) is not required at SAIL I-II, Medium at SAIL III, High at SAIL IV-VI.
notes: OSO#24 who defines conditions not shown

instrument: UK CAA Regulatory Library - OSO 24 (AMC to Reg (EU) 2019/947 Art 11, Annex E)
requirement_paraphrase: Medium: design UAS to perform in environmental conditions in the flight manual, with evidence; if simulation is used, justify the target environment. High: develop to a standard acceptable to the CAA, evidence assessed by CAA.
notes: Conditions from flight manual; simulation to be justified

instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Art 60
requirement_paraphrase: Real-world testing outside sandboxes needs a testing plan submitted to and approved by the market surveillance authority; silence after 30 days counts as approval only where national law provides for tacit approval, otherwise authorisation is still required. Testing lasts up to six months, extendable once by six months, with informed consent, reversible outputs and Art 73 incident reporting.

instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) Art 15
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk AI must achieve appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity; accuracy metrics declared in instructions for use; resilience to errors and inconsistencies in the system or environment; feedback-loop mitigation for continuing-learning systems.
notes: Robustness to environment stated, evidence form unclear

instrument: UAE GCAA CAAP 22 Incident Reporting
clause_or_section_seen: Sec 4-5, 5.8; Appendix B Sec VII and VI.13
requirement_paraphrase: Sets reporting categories and times (ROSI within 72 h for Cat 1; 15 calendar days for Cat 2; immediate notice for accidents/serious incidents); Appendix B lists unlawful interference with GNSS and navigation errors as reportable examples.
notes: Reporting of interference, not evidence about hazard

instrument: UAE GCAA CAR-OCR Occurrence Reporting and Aircraft Accident & Incident Investigation Regulation
requirement_paraphrase: GCAA reporting page says accidents and serious incidents should be reported immediately to the Duty Investigator, and lists 'Drones or unlawful interference affecting aircraft safety' among other safety-critical events. It gives separate Safety and Security (AVSEC) duty-investigator contacts without stating which events go where, and cites AAIR and CAR-OCR (Issue 01, Jan 2025) as the legal framework, aligned with ICAO Annex 13.
notes: Unlawful interference reporting; GNSS not named

instrument: Dubai RTA executive regulations for Law No. 9 of 2023 (autonomous vehicles)
requirement_paraphrase: Per Gulf News (13 Dec 2025), autonomous vehicles must meet seven technical and operational criteria for approval, including a manufacturer's certificate of successful road trials in its country of origin or another jurisdiction, evidence of conformity with relevant UAE or Gulf standards, and operational tests in Dubai demonstrating safety under local climatic conditions, with trial data shared with the RTA and identified issues addressed. Operators must notify the RTA of technical faults immediately and maintain integrated, secure electronic records of all operational data that may not be altered or deleted without prior RTA approval.
notes: Local climatic conditions tested in Dubai; heat not named

instrument: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02 R4 (GNSS outage and alterations)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends recurrent training of flight crews and relevant ops personnel; assessing risks of losing onboard GNSS; before flights into known affected areas, ensuring GNSS-backup systems are not MEL-inoperative and MEL backups do not rely on GNSS; planning non-GNSS procedures where practical; verifying position by non-GNSS means and navaid availability (jamming); monitoring non-GNSS navaids/EPU and GNSS vs non-GNSS time (spoofing); using flight data monitoring where required.
notes: Recommended risk assessment by operators

instrument: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02 R4
requirement_paraphrase: Asks operators to file AIREPs for GNSS anomalies, report safety-impacting events under Reg (EU) 376/2014 and report suspected spoofing and higher-risk jamming to manufacturers.
notes: Event reporting only

instrument: EASA ETSO-C146e (GPS/SBAS airborne equipment)
requirement_paraphrase: Requires stand-alone GPS/SBAS equipment to meet RTCA DO-229E Section 2 (Class Gamma or Delta, DO-229E dated 15 Dec 2016) as modified by ETSO Appendices 2 and 4 (e.g. required Class Gamma path leg types; L1 C/A-code-only ranging and restricted data demodulation). New Section 1.8.3 on cybersecurity/GPS spoofing states it contains no new requirements; it recommends ('should') cross-checks and data-validity checks as guidance.
notes: No new requirements; should cross-checks as guidance

instrument: CASA (Australia) guidance on GNSS interference
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends not relying only on GNSS, cross-checking with other navigation sources, assessing interference likelihood on planned and diversion routes and having backup plans.
notes: Recommends assessing interference likelihood

instrument: UK CAA guidance on GNSS jamming (via SUAS News report)
requirement_paraphrase: Reports that CAA advises operators not to rely solely on satellite navigation during known jamming trials (be ready for alternatives such as dead reckoning), notes jamming can disable drone return-to-home and digital geofencing, and urges pilots to report jamming not announced in advance.

instrument: ICAO MID PBN SG/8 WP11 (UAE) GNSS anomalies
requirement_paraphrase: UAE reports GPS jamming affecting aircraft in the Emirates FIR (example 3 Oct 2023) and proposes updating state rules to require prompt action and mandatory reporting of interference, with ANSP reporting procedures.

instrument: ICAO MID CNS SG/14 WP05 (UAE) protecting surveillance data integrity against GNSS interference
requirement_paraphrase: UAE reports an increase in interference cases and suspected spoofing over two years; asks the meeting to encourage MID States to set up surveillance-integrity investigation frameworks and designate national focal points for GNSS interference reporting, and to ask the ICAO MID Office to maintain a regional repository of reports.

instrument: ICAO Assembly A41-WP/196 (UAE) GNSS interference
requirement_paraphrase: UAE paper A41-WP/196 asks ICAO to bring the operational impact of GNSS interference to States' attention and urges States to implement the mitigation measures in Doc 9849; the three-step process (monitor, assess, mitigate) is described in the body, not named in the requested actions.

instrument: ICAO MID CNS SG/15 WP08 (Saudi Arabia) national GNSS monitoring
requirement_paraphrase: Proposes a national GNSS signal monitoring and reporting system for the Jeddah FIR and a regional RFI database.

instrument: RICS article: GNSS spoofing and mitigation in the Arabian Gulf
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends machine-control and robotic users configure alarms for coordinate jumps, fuse GNSS with IMU/LiDAR, use authenticated corrections, keep RTK fallback and validate time sync; surveyors to use multi-session observations and cross-checks.
notes: Design measures recommended, no evidence asked

instrument: IEC 60529 Degrees of protection (IP Code)
requirement_paraphrase: Classifies enclosure protection against solids/water; scope leaves corrosion, fungus and solar radiation to the product standard; lists IEC 60068-2-68 (dust and sand) as a normative reference.
notes: IP classes; dust test only a normative reference

instrument: IEC 60068-2-2 Environmental testing - Dry heat
requirement_paraphrase: Specifies dry-heat tests for heat-dissipating and non-dissipating specimens to see if equipment can be used, transported or stored at high temperature; severities in Table 1 not visible in preview.
notes: Dry heat test named; Table 1 severities not seen

instrument: ISO 3691-4 Industrial trucks - driverless trucks and systems
requirement_paraphrase: Table of contents shows climatic-condition and high-temperature clauses; requirement text not accessed.
notes: Title only; clause text not accessed

requirement_paraphrase: Preview states the document does not address requirements and tests for outdoor application. requirement_paraphrase: Adds safety requirements for robots used by or near general consumers, 'where applicable' covering indoor and outdoor locations; catalogue text does not mention temperature or dust.
notes: Catalogue text silent on temperature and dust
